info.title: Evictions API
info.description: Submit and track an eviction case for a rental property in any US state or DC. Evictions API is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. After a live case is submitted we engage a licensed attorney in the property's state for it; nothing is served on a tenant or filed in court until that attorney has reviewed the case, and the attorney serves and files through their own accounts while the case shows its status, documents, deadlines, messages and charges. Test keys are a free developer feature for building and testing an integration: a test key works only with a fictional test state (ZZ), and nothing real is served or filed. A built-in test reviewer approves test cases automatically once they enter review, and `POST /v1/cases/{id}/advance` moves a test case on one step at a time. A request in live mode on a server where live mode is off answers 403 `live_unavailable`. POST requests accept an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: Whether a jurisdiction is served, and its notice rules

200.description: Served status, `handling`, jurisdiction ids and the grounds. With a live key every US state and DC is served with `handling: "attorney_direct"`, `action: null` and, for each ground, `notice: null` and the facts intake requires (`requiredFacts`) and, where `fullService` is true, the facts that place's documents ask for beyond them (`documentFacts`: `notice` and `filing`, by where the case starts, and `conditional`, facts asked for only when another holds, and `defaults`, the pack's own default where a fact has one). They apply only to a case created with `service: "full"`: ask an attorney-path case for the intake facts alone; anything else is `served: false`. With a test key (`handling: "automated"`) the fictional test state answers with its notice rules for each ground. `fullService` says whether a case created here with `service: "full"` is handled by us as your agent (no attorney reviews it); where it is false, a managed-service request answers 409 `service_unavailable` with its operational reason. This does not establish a legal requirement for counsel.

post.summary: Read a lease (PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 4 MB and, for a PDF, 40 pages, as base64) with an AI service (Claude Haiku 4.5 through OpenRouter) and answer the facts the new-case form takes. For a file the free reading on the device could not read. With `kind: "correspondence"` and `files` (1 to 10 messages with the tenant: PDF, JPEG, PNG, plain text `text/plain`, or a saved email `message/rfc822` (`.eml`, at most 1 MB, turned into its text before it is sent); 8 MB, 40 PDF pages and 200,000 characters of text in all), it drafts what happened for a lease-violation case (`violationDescription`, `violationDate`): a draft for the person to read and correct, never a checked answer. One request counts once against the hourly limit, whatever the number of files. With `kind: "ledger"` and one `file` (a tenant ledger PDF, at most 4 MB and 40 pages), it answers the ledger's rows (`rows`, each `{ date, type: "charge" | "payment", amountCents, memo }`, at most 500, in the order printed) a balance brought forward from before them (`openingBalanceCents`, null when none) and the ending balance the ledger states (`endingBalanceCents`, null when it states none), for the caller to check: the balance brought forward and the rows should add up to the ending balance, and the website fills in nothing when they do not. A row dated after today is left out. The files are sent to OpenRouter only for this one reading, under fixed names (the `name` you send is never passed on), on endpoints that keep no data; nothing is stored and nothing of the files or the answer is logged. Every answer is a suggestion for a person to check: a fact the reading is unsure of is left out, never guessed. When the service refuses, fails or takes over 30 seconds, the answer is empty (`{ "suggestions": {}, "confidence": {} }`, or for a ledger `{ "rows": [], "openingBalanceCents": null, "endingBalanceCents": null }`), never an error. For now only the signed-in app and test keys can use it: a live API key answers 503 `extract_unavailable`. At most 20 an hour per organization (429 `rate_limited`); 503 `extract_unavailable` when the server has no AI service set

200.description: The answers found, in the same shape as the website's lease reading: each a `{ value, source: "lease_file" }` (`source: "messages"` for the messages' draft), and how sure the reading is of each (`high` or `medium`). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, `monthlyRent` is dollars with cents ("1450.00"), `noticePeriod` is whole days ("3"), `state` is the two-letter code; `parties` lists the landlord (`plaintiff`) and the tenants (`defendant`). From messages: `violationDescription` (a few plain sentences, at most 2,000 characters) and `violationDate` (never later than today).

amountCents.description: Whole cents, always positive; `type` says which way it moves the balance.

openingBalanceCents.description: A balance brought forward from before the first row, in whole cents (negative for a credit); null when the ledger shows none. It is not among `rows`.

endingBalanceCents.description: The balance the ledger states at its end, in whole cents (negative for a credit); null when it states none. `openingBalanceCents` plus the rows should come to it.

400.description: The request is invalid (`invalid_request`): `kind` must be `lease` or `ledger` with one `file`, or `correspondence` with `files` (1 to 10), and each file must have exactly `name`, `contentType` and `contentBase64` (valid base64).

SessionToken.description: A session token (`ess_...`) from `POST /v1/auth/signup` or `/v1/auth/login`, valid for 30 days. On the case, webhook, API key and organization routes it acts for the user's organization in the mode named by the `X-Evictions-Mode` header: `test` (the default) or `live`.

AttorneyToken.description: A user token (`eut_...`) of a verified attorney.

state.description: Position in the case lifecycle, for example `notice_review` or `filing_submitted`.

handling.description: Who does the legal work. `attorney_direct`: a licensed attorney engaged for the case reviews it, serves the notice and files in court, and the platform records each step; it is what a live case is unless the full-service path is open for its property. `automated`: the built-in test pipeline of a test case. `agent_filed`, the full-service path, as we describe it to the owner: We act as your authorized agent. No attorney reviews the case. We are not a law firm and do not give legal advice. Full service is available only in test mode for now; a case is created with it only when `POST /v1/cases` asks for `service: "full"` and that path is open for the property, and it needs the owner's signed authorization (`/v1/cases/{id}/authorization`).

attorney.description: The attorney engaged for an attorney-direct case, once recorded. Null until then, and always null for a test case.

barNumber.description: The attorney's bar number in that state.

erased.description: Whether the details of the case were erased, which we do case by case on request. An erased case keeps its id, state, dates, deadline names and charges. In `data` the names and the address read `[erased]` (the state and county are kept) and every other fact is gone; `courtCaseNumber` is null; each document keeps its id and `contentHash`, its `filename` reads `[erased]` and downloading it answers 410 `erased`; messages read `[erased]`. Any request that would change the case answers 409 `erased`.

erasedAt.description: When the details were erased. Null for a case that was not erased.

sources.description: Where each answer came from, by field path (`property.line1`, `lease.monthlyRentCents`, `parties.0`, `ledger`): the kind of source, and for a file read the id of the case document it was read from. An answer with no entry was typed. Empty when no answer came from a source. Never holds a value. Send `sources` with `POST /v1/cases` or `PATCH /v1/cases/{id}` to set it (a patch replaces the whole map); a patch that changes an answer without sending `sources` removes that answer's entry.

documentId.description: The case document the answer was read from (`lease_file`, `ledger_file` and `messages` only).

agent.description: Present, and true, only for an agent-filed case (`handling: "agent_filed"`): we act as your authorized agent, no attorney reviews the case, and we are not a law firm and do not give legal advice. Every field below appears only with it.

authorization.description: Whether your authorization for us to act as your agent is signed, and whether the facts changed after it was signed (then nothing more is done until you sign again).

complaintSignature.description: Whether the court requires the owner to sign the complaint, and whether the current complaint is signed. While it is required and unsigned, the case waits in `filing_approved`.

tasks.description: Each outward step of the case, oldest first (as `GET /v1/cases/{id}/tasks`).

checking.description: Present while we check what the next step sends before it is sent (we check every notice, filing and summons for now): `notice` (the notice to the tenant), `filing` (the court filing) or `summons`. Nothing is sent, and nothing is charged for that step, until it is checked.

sentBack.description: Present while the case is on hold because we checked a step before sending it and sent the case back to you: nothing was sent. `note` says why; reply by email, or withdraw the case.

claim.description: What the complaint asks the court for besides possession: unpaid rent, where the court lets us claim it as your agent, up to the court's limit where it has one.

amountClaimedCents.description: US cents. Zero when no rent is claimed.

hearing.description: The hearing, once the court has set one (or moved it): where the court requires the owner to attend in person (`clientAttends`), you must attend it yourself.

time.description: The court's local time, HH:MM, when known.

place.description: Where the court sits for the hearing, when known.

purpose.description: What an uploaded file (`kind: "evidence"`) is for, as given with the upload. Null for documents the platform or the attorney adds, and for files uploaded before purposes were kept.

contentType.description: Decided from the file's first bytes when it was stored, never from its name. `text/plain` only for a `correspondence` document that is plain text (the body of a forwarded email).

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the document bytes. An attorney approval names these.

PmsConnection.description: The organization's stored connection to a property-management system. Its credentials are kept encrypted and never returned.

label.description: The name the organization gave it; the system's name by default.

lastError.description: How the last search or pull failed (`unauthorized`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`); null when it worked.

LeaseMatch.description: A lease a search found, as the property-management system holds it. Empty strings where it has nothing to show.

name.description: The system's own name for the lease (DoorLoop).

balanceCents.description: What the system says the tenant owes.

PmsPull.description: One lease read from the property-management system as suggested answers for a new case (each `{ value, source }`, the source being the system), the lease PDF when the system holds one, and the system's balance to check the ledger rows against. Nothing of it is stored: the person checks every answer.

skippedRows.description: How many ledger rows were left out because their transaction type is not one we map. Absent when none.

IntakeFile.description: A file waiting in the organization's intake inbox for a case: a PDF, JPEG or PNG the customer already has, or the plain text of a forwarded email. It waits 30 days, then is deleted unless it was moved onto a case.

source.description: How it arrived: forwarded by email, or sent through the API (an AI agent or an integration).

contentType.description: Decided from the file's first bytes, never from its name. `text/plain` only for the text of a forwarded email, stored by us.

purposeGuess.description: What the file is probably for: as sent, or guessed from its name. Confirmed when it is moved onto a case.

note.description: The email's subject or the sender's note; null when none.

expiresAt.description: When the file is deleted if it has not been moved onto a case.

Charge.description: An amount owed to the platform for a case: the platform fee, or court or service costs passed on at cost. The attorney's legal fee is never a charge here: it is separate and paid to the attorney.

collection.description: How the charge is paid. `checkout`: on the payment page (`POST /v1/cases/{id}/charges/{chargeId}/checkout`). `automatic`: a cost of a full-service case, taken from the saved card (`/v1/payment-method`); it is never paid by checkout.

PaymentMethod.description: The card saved for the automatic charges of full-service cases, in the key's mode: its brand and last four only. `failed`: the card was declined, and the cases waiting on a payment stay on hold until a new card is saved.

Note.description: A message on a case, between the customer and the platform.

Authorization.description: The authorization the owner signs for an agent-filed case: the text to sign now, the signature in force for it, and whether the case facts changed after it was signed. A change to the facts makes the signature stale until the owner signs again.

textVersion.description: The version of the text, recorded with every signature.

text.description: The text the owner signs: plain text, numbered paragraphs.

stale.description: True when the facts changed after the signature. The case does not proceed until it is signed again.

Signature.description: A signature the owner just gave. The IP address it was given from is kept only as a hash, and is not shown.

ComplaintToSign.description: The complaint documents the owner signs where the county requires the owner to sign the complaint itself, and whether exactly this set is signed.

Task.description: One outward step of a full-service case (`handling: "agent_filed"`): delivering the notice, filing, ordering the summons, attending the hearing, a signature from the owner, or mail from the court.

dueAt.description: When the step must be done by, when there is a deadline.

action.description: The proposed act the answer is about.

declared.description: Whether the customer declared these facts, and not only a suggestion.

declaredAt.description: When the customer declared them last.

problem.description: Why the stored facts do not read as a complete declaration.

missing.description: The facts this act is missing, each with the question to ask. An empty list is not permission to perform the act.

sources.description: Where each declared fact came from: the source of the last write that set it, `customer` or `suggestion`. A fact that is absent was never declared by anyone.

Filing.description: A submission to the court. Attorney-only.

rejectionReasons.description: The court's reasons, when it rejected the filing.

ServiceAttempt.description: One request to serve a document on one defendant. Attorney-only.

failureReason.description: The process server's reason, when service failed.

Attention.description: Whether the case needs the attorney: it is on hold, or a job for it failed for good after its last state change.

AttorneyCase.description: The case as its assigned attorney sees it. Each read is recorded in the audit log as `tenant_data_viewed`.

events.description: The full audit trail, including internal events.
